name: Trip.com Group Limited
moat_justification: China's dominant online travel platform (Ctrip, Qunar, Trip.com, Skyscanner) with scale in hotel/airline supply, service infrastructure and data — but the SAMR antitrust decision in July 2026 directly outlawed the exclusivity and lowest-price tactics that reinforced that dominance, consumers multi-home across Meituan, Fliggy, Tongcheng and Douyin at near-zero switching cost, and suppliers are now explicitly freed to multi-home.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CNY converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Trip.com Group Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-28), cover / Item 4: American depositary shares (each representing one ordinary share, par value US$0.00125 per share), symbol TCOM on Nasdaq; the FY2025 results release likewise states each ADS currently represents one ordinary share of the Company) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.0x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Dominant China OTA, moat 6/10, net cash — but growth decelerated to +6% YoY in Q2 2026, OE/share has fallen two years, and SAMR rectification bans its exclusivity tactics: weighted IRR 14.5%, weighted IV@15 $37.76 vs $39.37 price; clears 15% only at/below ~$37.76.
moat_for: Dominant China OTA scale: Ctrip/Qunar/Trip.com/Skyscanner brand portfolio, deepest hotel and airline supply, go-to destination for Asian travelers
One-stop platform + service infrastructure (24/7 support, AI/data from accumulated travel insights) that smaller rivals cannot match at scale
International platform compounding fast: international revenue +50%+ YoY in Q2 2026 and inbound bookings +95% YoY in H1 2026, diversifying beyond China
Fortress liquidity: cash, equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments of RMB105.8B at Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025 results release), engine net debt is negative (net cash)
moat_against: SAMR antitrust rectification (July 2026): exclusivity deals and lowest-price demands — core moat tactics — are banned; multi-tier partner framework replaces them, weakening pricing/supply lock-in

Near-zero consumer switching costs: Meituan, Fliggy (Alibaba), Tongcheng and Douyin compete for the same bookings and are now themselves under regulatory scrutiny, intensifying service-based competition
Regulatory/political overhang in China: dominant-position abuse finding since 2020, US class action followed, and further compliance adjustments were guided to weigh on margins
Supplier pushback: hotels/airlines regain pricing autonomy and multi-homing rights, pressuring take rates
